body:
Every ticket needs a boundary before work starts, and today every one is written by hand. That holds for a couple of items and not for a sprint.

Problem: producing a boundary is manual every time, so the practice lasts only while someone has the patience for it.
Goal: a person receives a drafted boundary built from the refined criteria, and decides whether it freezes.

Acceptance criteria:
- When the refined criteria become ready, a person is asked whether to draft the boundary, and nothing is drafted until they agree.
- A reviewer given a drafted boundary names no entry they had to write themselves.
- Refined criteria the drafter cannot produce a boundary from leave the issue recording each missing thing separately, and no boundary is produced.
- Each recorded blocker names the missing criterion or the undecided question, and can be resolved without resolving the others.
- Resolving the last blocker produces a new drafted boundary without anyone being asked again.
- A boundary written or edited by hand freezes without any step a drafted one does not require.
- Every frozen boundary carries a recorded approval by a person.

Out of scope:
- Reducing how much a person reviews. Separate item, blocked on measuring what review costs.
- The boundary's shape. It may change to suit the agent stage; this item neither requires nor prevents that.
- Producing the refined criteria. That is the upstream stage.
title: Draft the boundary from the refined criteria
